static_traits.name: Lin Wen
static_traits.family_status: Living in an apartment with four siblings and a mother who teaches
static_traits.social_status: Has family support resources (mother and siblings), but has not yet discussed the distress with family; interpersonal situation not disclosed
static_traits.medical_history: Without significant physical illness; has not received psychotherapy before; similar art-related problems had not appeared before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fair cooperation, but negative tone; often using absolutist and negating expressions (such as 'I am not good enough''should give up'); skeptical about positive feedback

basic_info.main_problem: Sense of frustration and failure related to painting: believing one is unable to sell works, thus shaking the will to continue creating, with thoughts of giving up; worsened when seeing other artists succeed and receive praise, with increased self-doubt and depression.
basic_info.core_demands: Negative thoughts and feelings have begun to affect creative motivation and cause distress, affecting daily life, so she seeks counseling to relieve these troubles.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough(as an Artist)
The value of my work (and my value) depends on external recognition and sales

special_situations.event: Long unable to sell any works
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the works have not been sold, it means they have no value, I am just a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forcibly tying creative value to sales; considering stopping creation when sales remain absent to avoid further failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Not being able to sell proves I am bad, I should give up

special_situations.event: Seeing other artists posting successes and receiving likes on social media
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach their level or acclaim, it means I am not good enough, I will not succeed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly comparing with others, doubling practice to try to prove oneself; when still feeling inferior after comparing, tending to withdraw or wanting to give up
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never reach their level

special_situations.event: Friends giving positive reviews of one's work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Positive feedback does not count, only sales or wide recognition is true evaluation
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating praise, ignoring positive cues, keeping only evidence consistent with failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite, my works are actually not valuable

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If it ultimately cannot be sold, this creation is a waste of time
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-denial before starting work, reducing investment or procrastinating or even stopping creation, to reduce the sense of 'meaninglessness' and failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No one will buy this painting, making it is futile anyway

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen and recognized, gaining value and a sense of achievement as an artist
core_conflict.fear: Afraid of being negated and failing, worrying one will never reach others' standards, being seen as not good enough
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being humiliated and failing through withdrawal, negating positive feedback, and tying value to sales

object_relations.object_representation: Picky others/audiences who only recognize sales and fame

object_relations.self_representation: A dependent who needs external proof of worth
object_relations.object_representation: Others who may look down on or not understand oneself (such as online audiences, potential buyers)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor probes and reinforces the friend's positive feedback, inviting the client to consider its authenticity and meaning
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding others' praise as insincere or inconsistent with reality (not yet sold)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a skeptical and negating tone, emphasizing 'they are just being polite', keeping distance from praise.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests exploring the value of art beyond sales (such as creating for loved ones)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding creation 'not aimed at sales' as having no meaning, not worth investing in
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing 'if it does not sell it has no value' with causal, absolutist expressions, firm tone to maintain existing beliefs.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether they are willing to share current emotional distress and creative pressure with family
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Presetting that family will consider one's distress 'childish / unimportant', thus choosing not to express it
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Keeps silent or understates, avoids unfolding feeling details, tone is restrained.

manifestations: Binds the value of art entirely to sales and external praise
When starting a new work, feels 'doing it is in vain anyway'
Difficulty accepting positive feedback, believing that not selling means not valuable
outcomes: The creative process shifting from pleasure to pressure and a sense of meaninglessness

manifestations: Though having family support resources, choosing not to share the distress with mother and siblings
When comparing with others' success on social media, self-isolation and inferiority intensify
outcomes: Lacks realistic emotional support and corrective experiences

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Directly takes the social standard 'only what sells has value' as the sole standard for measuring oneself and one's work
Defining self-worth by sales and praise

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Considering the friend's praise as merely polite, insincere
Projecting inner self-doubt and unworthiness onto others as their contempt for oneself

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent self-blame and self-denial ('I am not good enough')
Overly cautious about sharing troubles, carefully avoids seeking help

positive_force: Stable love of painting and practice commitment (long-term practice)
Having potential family support resources (mother and four siblings)
negative_force: Excessively relying on external validation (sales and praise) to define worth
Inferiority and despair triggered by comparing with others
Black-and-white thinking directly equating 'not yet sold' with 'failure'
Negating positive feedback, keeping only negative evidence (mental filtering and negating the positive)
Making negative predictions when starting to create, increasing stress and avoidance

target_behavior.behavior: Strong self-denial and thoughts of giving up in creation-related situations
antecedent: Seeing other artists posting successes and receiving likes on social media
target_behavior.core_reason: Tying self-worth to work sales, driven by comparison and despair and black-and-white thinking; tending to withdraw to avoid shame and failure
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential failure and being negated, briefly relieving anxiety and shame
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased creative motivation, reduced investment, low mood and intensifying self-doubt

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding seeking help and expressing emotional distress (not discussing with family)
antecedent: Thinking about family's possible views or reactions
When feeling frustrated and self-doubt worsens
target_behavior.core_reason: Negative predictions and mind-reading about others' reactions (worrying about being looked down on), accompanied by shame and self-denial
target_behavior.function: Avoids being judged and emotional exposure, maintaining surface safety
target_behavior.consequence: Lacking real support and corrective feedback, increased sense of isolation, negative emotions persisting

target_behavior.behavior: Negating positive feedback, interpreting praise as insincere
antecedent: Friends' positive comments and encouragement on the work
target_behavior.core_reason: The negative core belief 'I am not good enough' and the cognitive bias from external-validation preference (negating the positive, mental filtering)
target_behavior.function: Maintains a negative self-schema to avoid cognitive dissonance
target_behavior.consequence: Self-esteem further damaged, positive cues unable to be internalized, depression and anxiety levels rising
